topStories.headline: Downtown's Numbers Hit New Highs — But the Tenderloin Asks: What About Us?
topStories.dek: A new SF Standard investigation finds that the wave of private investment reshaping the Financial District and Union Square has yet to reach the Tenderloin and Mid-Market, even as the Downtown Development Corporation pledges $60 million to the city's core.
topStories.body:
San Francisco's downtown recovery is showing up in hard data. The Downtown SF Partnership's Q2 2026 Market Report, published this month on downtownsf.org, recorded a record 10.54 million non-resident visits, hotel revenue per available room up 15.8 percent year over year, and falling office vacancy across all building classes. Average daily visits to the Financial District and Jackson Square were up 34.7 percent over Q4 2025, a surge the Partnership attributes to major events and new ground-floor openings.

But a September 7 investigation by the San Francisco Standard found that almost all of that private momentum — and nearly all of the Downtown Development Corporation's pledged $60 million — is flowing to Union Square, the Embarcadero, the East Cut, and Yerba Buena. The DDC, a nonprofit that funnels private money into public projects, was launched last year. City planners told stakeholders that the organization selects projects where public bond money is already available to match private investment, which is the case for the Powell Street improvement and Embarcadero Plaza projects now moving toward construction.

For the Tenderloin and Mid-Market, that logic stings. Kate Robinson, head of the Tenderloin Community Benefit District, has been leading community leaders on tours of her neighborhood's improvements — new decorative gates, monthly street parties on Larkin — to show what sustained investment could do there. 'The sky is the limit for the need,' she said, according to the Standard. Advocates argue their neighborhoods are essential to downtown's full recovery but remain structurally cut off from the investment wave.

The dynamic highlights a tension that will likely persist as downtown's renaissance accelerates: whether the benefits of recovery, however real, reach beyond the blocks that were already most attractive to private capital.

topStories.headline: Embarcadero Plaza Overhaul Cleared to Break Ground This Fall — Here's What the $40 Million Park Will Look Like
topStories.dek: The San Francisco Recreation and Park Commission unanimously approved the final design for the $40 million Embarcadero Plaza waterfront park in June, with construction targeted for late 2026.
topStories.body:
The foot of Market Street is about to look very different. On June 18, 2026, the San Francisco Recreation and Park Commission unanimously approved a final concept design — produced by architecture firm HOK — for a sweeping overhaul of Embarcadero Plaza and the adjacent Sue Bierman Park. The $40 million public-private project would transform the combined five-acre site into a cohesive park anchored by an expansive central lawn, playground, community gathering space, and outdoor dining area.

The redesign would also replace the controversial Vaillancourt Fountain — long a source of debate — with new green space. Mayor Daniel Lurie described the project as turning the site into 'a true front door to downtown and a destination in its own right.' HOK's San Francisco-based planning director Brian Jencek called it an 'iconic, connective waterfront experience.' Construction is projected to begin in late 2026 and take roughly a year to complete, according to the San Francisco Recreation and Park Department.

Funding is split between public bond money and private sources. Supervisor Danny Sauter introduced legislation in June for the city to accept up to $20 million in private funding, formalizing the role of the San Francisco Downtown Development Corporation in building the park. The Downtown SF Partnership, the Downtown Development Corp., and the city's Office of Economic and Workforce Development are all participating in fundraising. The park, once built, will be managed by Rec and Park and will host festivals, concerts, picnic areas, and gardens designed to connect the Embarcadero waterfront to the Financial District core.

topStories.headline: Ferry Building's Final Vacant Suites Are Finally Filling Up — Including a New Mediterranean Restaurant
topStories.dek: Restaurateur Kaïs Bouzidi's Hayati and Shelley Lindgren's Lucania are the two most-watched openings as the Ferry Building approaches full occupancy for the first time since 2020.
topStories.body:
After years of pandemic-era vacancies, the Ferry Building is approaching full occupancy. Two of its highest-profile incoming restaurants — Hayati and Lucania — are both expected to open in the second half of 2026, completing a transformation that has also seen the building push into evening programming and longer hours.

Hayati, from Paris-born restaurateur Kaïs Bouzidi of Sens, Barcha, and Bon Délire, will take over the former Boulettes Larder space in Suite 48 at the back of the building. Bouzidi describes the concept as a 'Middle Eastern concept, from the food to the spirit and the design,' offering daily lunch, happy hour, and dinner. He has said he plans to keep the bones of the Boulettes Larder space — including a wood-burning oven — while overhauling the design for a 'chic and vibey' feel. Hayati would be Bouzidi's fourth restaurant within a few blocks of the Ferry Building, adding to Sens at Embarcadero Center, Barcha in the Financial District, and Bon Délire at Pier 3.

Also coming to the building is Lucania, a southern Italian restaurant from Shelley Lindgren, the James Beard Award-winning owner of A16. Lindgren secured the large former MarketBar space, which will feature a 140-seat outdoor patio and is targeting a second-half-2026 opening. A third newcomer, Arquet from the team behind Soma restaurant Sorrel, will focus on California cuisine. Foot traffic at the Ferry Building rose 23 percent year over year in the first quarter of 2025, its strongest opening quarter on record, according to an analysis published earlier this year — a sign that San Franciscans are treating the building as a dinner destination again, not just a lunchtime stop.

events.title: Pickwick Vintage Show at the Ferry Building
events.description: More than 40 local vendors fill the Ferry Building mezzanine with curated vintage clothing, fine jewelry, accessories, and textiles. Tickets are ticketed in advance and often sell out; limited walk-up availability in the afternoon.

events.title: People in Plazas: Soul/Funk Free Lunchtime Concert
events.description: Part of the free annual People in Plazas series, this lunchtime concert brings local professional musicians to the plaza at 555 California with a soul and funk set. Free, no RSVP required.

events.title: Waterfront Walkabout — Free SF Art Stroll (Launch Night)
events.location: Ferry Building North Plaza to the Exploratorium, Embarcadero
events.description: The inaugural edition of a new monthly series launching September 17: live music, interactive pop-ups, oysters, and drinks at the Ferry Building's front plaza, then a guided stroll past four large-scale sculptures along the Big Art Loop – Portside trail. Returns every third Thursday this fall. Free; separate tickets for Exploratorium After Dark.

events.title: People in Plazas: Country Concert at Rincon Center
events.description: A free outdoor lunchtime country concert inside the People in Plazas summer series, held at Rincon Center near the Embarcadero. One of more than 130 concerts running through September across Financial District and Embarcadero plazas.

events.title: Oktoberfest on Front — Free Financial District Block Party
events.location: 240 Front Street, Financial District Entertainment Zone
events.description: Co-hosted by the Downtown SF Partnership and Schroeder's, San Francisco's annual Oktoberfest block party returns to the Front Street Entertainment Zone with live Bavarian polka by Ladyhosen, party hits by Pop Rocks, beer hall games, over 70 beers on tap from Schroeder's, Harrington's, and Royal Exchange, and German food specials. Free to attend.

moreNews.headline: Downtown SF Partnership's Q2 2026 Report Records Best-Ever Visitor Numbers
moreNews.body: The Downtown SF Partnership published its Q2 2026 Market Report this fall, showing non-resident district visits hitting a record 10.54 million and hotel revenue per available room up 15.8 percent year over year. The Partnership, which covers the Financial District and Jackson Square, also reported falling office vacancy across all building classes. The report credits major events and new ground-floor business openings for the surge, and notes that average daily visits were up 34.7 percent over Q4 2025.

moreNews.headline: San Francisco Retail Vacancy Falls Below 6% for First Time Since 2023
moreNews.body: Citywide retail vacancy fell to 5.8 percent in Q2 2026, down from 6.3 percent in Q1 and 6.9 percent a year ago, according to Cushman & Wakefield's Q2 2026 MarketBeat report released in August. It marks the first time the rate has dropped below 6 percent since Q2 2023. Visitor volumes are projected to reach 24.2 million in 2026, with spending expected to hit a record $9.9 billion, surpassing the city's pre-pandemic peak — a tailwind for retailers in Union Square and along the Embarcadero.

restaurants.name: Wayfare Tavern
restaurants.description: Chef Tyler Florence's flagship San Francisco tavern — now at a larger location on Pine Street — serves timeless American dishes in a dramatic two-floor space with marble floors, tufted leather booths, and a gold-leaf mural.

restaurants.name: Boulevard
restaurants.description: Chef Nancy Oakes's landmark Embarcadero restaurant occupies the historic Audiffred Building and has served refined California cuisine with bay views since 1993.

restaurants.name: Waterbar
restaurants.description: Waterbar offers sustainably sourced fish and shellfish — including one of the West Coast's most extensive oyster selections — with panoramic Bay Bridge views from the Embarcadero waterfront.

restaurants.name: Historic John's Grill
restaurants.description: San Francisco's legendary steakhouse since 1908, made famous by Dashiell Hammett's 'The Maltese Falcon,' serving classic steaks, seafood, and cocktails with live jazz seven nights a week.

restaurants.name: Bix
restaurants.description: A glamorous Art Deco-inspired supper club tucked in a historic Jackson Square alley, known for nightly live jazz, classic cocktails, and refined modern American cuisine.

restaurants.name: Ama by Brad Kilgore
restaurants.description: A chic 'Itameshi' jewel-box in Jackson Square blending Italian and Japanese technique through handcrafted pastas, koji-aged meats, sashimi, and creative cocktails.

restaurants.name: Mastro's Steakhouse
restaurants.description: A premier steakhouse near Union Square offering prime-aged cuts, fresh seafood, and tableside presentations in an elegant, high-energy setting.

restaurants.name: La Mar Cocina Peruana
restaurants.description: Chef Gastón Acurio's celebrated Peruvian concept brings ceviche, tiraditos, and anticuchos to the Embarcadero waterfront with sweeping bay views.

restaurants.name: Per Diem
restaurants.description: A lively all-day restaurant and bar popular with the Financial District lunch and happy-hour crowd, serving California-inspired cuisine and craft cocktails.

restaurants.name: Orafo
restaurants.description: An upscale Italian restaurant in the Financial District drawing consistent praise for handmade pastas and a well-curated wine list.

restaurants.name: Hog Island Oyster Co. – Ferry Building
restaurants.description: The flagship bar of Marin County's celebrated oyster farm, serving Tomales Bay bivalves, Dungeness crab, and California wines inside the Ferry Building.

restaurants.name: Gott's Roadside – Ferry Building
restaurants.description: A beloved Bay Area institution serving classic burgers, shakes, and fried chicken sandwiches from a counter inside the Ferry Building.

restaurants.name: The Rotunda at Neiman Marcus
restaurants.description: San Francisco's most theatrical lunch spot, set beneath an ornate stained-glass dome in the Union Square Neiman Marcus, famous for its popovers and afternoon tea service.

restaurants.name: Sam's Grill & Seafood Restaurant
restaurants.description: A Financial District institution since 1867, Sam's Grill is San Francisco's oldest restaurant, offering classic seafood and American dishes in curtained booths favored by generations of FiDi regulars.

restaurants.name: Mikkeller Bar San Francisco
restaurants.description: The San Francisco outpost of the Danish craft brewery, offering an ever-rotating tap list of rare and experimental beers in a bright, relaxed space near Civic Center.

restaurants.name: Café de la Presse
restaurants.description: A European-style café and newsstand at the corner of Grant and Bush near Union Square, serving espresso, pastries, and French-inspired food alongside an international press rack.

restaurants.name: Bocadillos
restaurants.description: A lively tapas and pintxos bar in the Financial District serving Basque-inspired small plates and Spanish wines in a casual, convivial setting popular for after-work gatherings.

restaurants.name: The Bird
restaurants.description: A beloved downtown quick-serve spot famous for its juicy fried chicken sandwiches and fried chicken-topped waffles, drawing a long loyal following from FiDi workers.

restaurants.name: Mixt
restaurants.description: A health-focused salad counter with multiple downtown locations, building customizable bowls from local, seasonal produce and quality proteins.

hotels.name: Palace Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel
hotels.description: A San Francisco landmark since 1875, the Palace Hotel features a sky-lit indoor pool, signature dining in the opulent Garden Court, and a history of hosting heads of state and Hollywood.

hotels.name: The Westin St. Francis San Francisco on Union Square
hotels.description: An iconic Union Square landmark since 1904, the Westin St. Francis is the only downtown hotel with cable cars stopping directly at its doors, offering historic Landmark Building rooms alongside a modern Tower Building.

hotels.name: Four Seasons Hotel San Francisco at Embarcadero
hotels.description: A sleek five-star property at the foot of the Financial District offering panoramic downtown and bay views, in-room massage services, and refined dining steps from the Embarcadero.

hotels.name: Hyatt Regency San Francisco
hotels.description: A flagship Hyatt property in Embarcadero Center with a dramatically renovated atrium, bay and city views, and Eclipse Kitchen & Bar, located steps from the Ferry Building.

hotels.name: Omni San Francisco Hotel
hotels.description: A 362-room luxury hotel housed in a historic Financial District building, consistently ranked among the city's top downtown hotels for its refined service and central location.

hotels.name: Hilton San Francisco Financial District
hotels.description: A 27-floor hotel in the Financial District with sweeping bay and city views, 20,000 square feet of event space, and Flyte Coffee Wine Bar on site.

hotels.name: Harbor Court Hotel
hotels.description: A non-smoking, eco-friendly boutique hotel nestled along the bay between the Financial District and Oracle Park, offering complimentary access to the adjacent YMCA fitness center.

hotels.name: Beacon Grand, A Union Square Hotel
hotels.description: A beautifully restored historic property at the corner of Powell and Sutter, offering art deco elegance with modern amenities and a prime cable car–adjacent location.

hotels.name: Club Quarters Hotel, Embarcadero
hotels.description: A centrally located business-oriented hotel near the Ferry Building offering streamlined, comfortable rooms and easy access to the Embarcadero and Financial District.

hotels.name: Hotel Nikko San Francisco
hotels.description: A 532-room Union Square property with a rooftop pool and fitness center, popular with both leisure and business travelers for its central location and extensive amenities.

shops.name: The Best Bookstore
shops.description: A curated independent bookstore that opened in late 2025 steps from the Powell Street cable car turnaround, bringing a literary presence back to Union Square with a downstairs author-events space.

shops.name: William Stout Architectural Books
shops.description: A world-renowned specialist bookstore in Jackson Square stocking an unparalleled selection of architecture, urban planning, photography, and design titles.

shops.name: Japonesque Gallery
shops.description: Koichi Hara's Jackson Square gallery showcases Japanese aesthetics from ancient to contemporary, selling fine art objects, ceramics, and decorative works with a discerning curatorial eye.

shops.name: Filson
shops.description: The Seattle heritage brand's Jackson Square outpost carries its full line of rugged bags, outerwear, and accessories built to last a lifetime, styled for both outdoors and city.

shops.name: A.P.C.
shops.description: The Parisian brand's San Francisco boutique brings its signature understated French style — clean denim, refined basics, and seasonal collaborations — to Jackson Square.

shops.name: Shinola
shops.description: The Detroit brand's Jackson Square shop offers handcrafted watches, leather goods, and bicycles made in the USA, in a thoughtfully designed boutique space.

shops.name: Eden & Eden
shops.description: A beloved Jackson Square shop curating an eclectic mix of jewelry, ceramics, art prints, and objects from independent makers worldwide.

shops.name: Allbirds
shops.description: The San Francisco-born sustainable shoe brand's Jackson Square flagship sells its wool and eucalyptus-fiber footwear and apparel with a focus on environmental transparency.

shops.name: Nintendo Store San Francisco
shops.description: Nintendo's newer flagship store on Powell Street offers the full range of Nintendo hardware, games, and character merchandise in an interactive, family-friendly retail environment.

shops.name: Moleskine
shops.description: The Italian brand's dedicated store near Union Square carries its full range of notebooks, planners, writing instruments, and accessories alongside limited-edition collaborations.

shops.name: Pop Mart
shops.description: The Beijing-based collectibles brand's Union Square location sells its popular blind-box art toys, large-format figures, and limited collaborations that draw dedicated collectors.

artEntertainment.name: SFMOMA – San Francisco Museum of Modern Art
artEntertainment.description: The West Coast's premier modern and contemporary art museum, currently presenting Jacob Hashimoto's Giant Arc (free, Floor 1) and RM x SFMOMA: Between You and Me opening October 3, alongside permanent collection galleries.

artEntertainment.name: Punch Line Comedy Club
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's oldest running comedy club, open since 1978 in the Financial District, presenting national headliners and emerging comedians in an intimate 182-seat room Tuesday through Sunday.

artEntertainment.name: American Conservatory Theater (A.C.T.) – Toni Rembe Theater
artEntertainment.description: San Francisco's premier regional theater company presents acclaimed productions of classics and new works in a beautifully restored 1910 Beaux-Arts building near Union Square.

artEntertainment.name: Scott Richards Contemporary Art
artEntertainment.description: A Jackson Square gallery representing a diverse roster of American and international contemporary painters and sculptors, with rotating exhibitions in airy historic brick spaces.

artEntertainment.name: Gallery Wendi Norris
artEntertainment.description: A respected Jackson Square gallery specializing in museum-quality modern and contemporary works from the Americas and Asia, with a strong program of solo exhibitions and art fairs.

artEntertainment.name: ICA SF – Institute of Contemporary Art San Francisco
artEntertainment.description: An artist-focused contemporary art institution presenting thought-provoking exhibitions and programs at its Financial District location at 345 Montgomery Street.

artEntertainment.name: Rebecca Camacho Presents
artEntertainment.description: An emerging and mid-career contemporary art gallery in Jackson Square known for championing experimental and boundary-pushing work across media.

artEntertainment.name: Crown Point Press
artEntertainment.type: Fine art print studio and gallery
artEntertainment.description: One of the world's leading fine art printmaking workshops, Crown Point Press has worked with artists including John Cage and Richard Diebenkorn; its gallery near Union Square shows prints by living and historical masters.

artEntertainment.name: 111 Minna Gallery
artEntertainment.description: A large-scale gallery and event venue in a former warehouse space near the Financial District, hosting rotating exhibitions of urban and contemporary art alongside public and private events.

artEntertainment.name: Exploratorium
artEntertainment.description: The world-famous hands-on science museum at Pier 15 on the Embarcadero invites visitors of all ages to explore the science of perception, nature, and human experience through hundreds of interactive exhibits.

gymsRecreation.name: Equinox Pine Street
gymsRecreation.description: Housed in the landmark 1915 Pacific Coast Stock Exchange building, Equinox's Financial District flagship offers a full club experience with group fitness, pilates, personal training, and premium locker rooms.

gymsRecreation.name: Bay Club Financial District
gymsRecreation.description: The Financial District location of the Bay Club offers a comprehensive fitness center, group exercise classes, pilates, yoga, and a sauna and steam room at 555 California Street.

gymsRecreation.name: BODYROK Financial District
gymsRecreation.description: A pilates-inspired 45-minute full-body strength training class on a custom BODYROK reformer, popular with downtown workers looking for an efficient midday or before-work workout.

gymsRecreation.name: Equinox Sports Club San Francisco
gymsRecreation.description: Equinox's largest San Francisco club on Market Street features a pool, multiple workout studios, a full range of group fitness classes, and a spa.

gymsRecreation.name: The Olympic Club
gymsRecreation.description: Founded in 1860, the Olympic Club is the oldest athletic club in the United States, offering members a full range of facilities including a pool, courts, and gymnasium in the heart of the Financial District.

gymsRecreation.name: Active Sports Club at Union Square
gymsRecreation.description: A well-equipped fitness center steps from Union Square featuring a three-lane pool, cardio machines, free weights, strength equipment, a steam room, and yoga studio space.

gymsRecreation.name: Rincon Park
gymsRecreation.description: A scenic Embarcadero-front green space on the south end of the waterfront near Rincon Hill, offering Bay Bridge views, a lawn, benches, and the famous 'Cupid's Span' bow-and-arrow sculpture by Claes Oldenburg.

gymsRecreation.name: Embarcadero Promenade
gymsRecreation.description: The scenic waterfront path stretching along San Francisco Bay from the Ferry Building toward Oracle Park, ideal for running, cycling, and walking with unobstructed views of the Bay Bridge and East Bay hills.

gymsRecreation.name: Barry's San Francisco – Financial District
gymsRecreation.description: The downtown location of the globally acclaimed HIIT studio combines treadmill intervals with floor strength work in a red-lit 'Red Room' popular with FiDi professionals.
